Since new software and new data were generated as part of the research goals (benchmarking a novel algorithm application), this falls into the Generated categories for both software and data.

This is a cluster randomized controlled trial that generated new primary data through assessments of mothers/children (pregnancy, 3, 6, 15, 24 months) across 8 clinics. This data collection is central to the research goals and constitutes newly generated data (D1). There is no mention of any software being developed or used in a substantial way to achieve the research goals - standard statistical analysis is implied but not highlighted as a research contribution, so it falls under No Software (S3).

These phenotype code lists represent newly generated data (coding lists) that are a research output shared for other researchers to use, going beyond mere use of existing data - they are a substantial, novel research product. The analysis itself uses standard statistical software (e.g., Stata/R for Poisson regression) but no new software tool or package is created or shared; only standard statistical analysis methods are applied, so software does not play a substantial 'generated' or even 'used-as-tool' role beyond routine analysis. Thus this is classified as no substantial software development (S3) combined with generation of new phenotype/code-list data used for analysis (D1).

This is a perspective/opinion piece on decolonising the psychology curriculum. It discusses conceptual and pedagogical issues without conducting empirical data collection or analysis, and does not develop, use, or reference any software tools as part of the research process.

The paper's main contribution is compiling a new global dataset (DOCU-CLIM) of 621 documentary climate time series, integrating published and previously unpublished records into a novel, shared dataset—clearly D1 (Data Generated). While the researchers perform proxy forward modeling and correlation analyses, there is no indication that they developed new software tools or substantially extended existing software as part of the research; standard statistical/correlation methods appear to be used without any described software development or release. Thus, software does not play a substantial, novel role, placing it in S3 (No Software).

The study generated new sediment core-derived multilocus metabarcoding biodiversity data spanning 100 years, combined with newly measured biocide and climate records - a substantial, novel dataset central to the research. They also developed a new conceptual/computational framework using explainable AI network models with multimodal learning specifically to link biodiversity dynamics with abiotic change, representing custom-developed software/analytical pipeline rather than merely applying existing off-the-shelf tools. Both the data (sediment eDNA metabarcoding time series, biocide measurements) and the analytical framework (explainable network models) were generated as part of this research and are central to achieving the research goals, making this S1D1.

It does not present new software tools or newly generated datasets; it synthesizes findings from prior studies without performing original data analysis or software development.

This is a review article discussing concepts and challenges in post-GWAS interpretation of AD and PD genetic risk loci in microglia. It does not generate or substantially use specific software tools or datasets itself; it synthesizes existing literature and discusses computational tools/datasets conceptually rather than performing original data analysis or software development.

This is a review article summarizing existing literature on MAIT cells and the microbiome. It does not generate or use any specific software tools, nor does it generate or analyze new datasets. It is purely a narrative synthesis of prior research findings.

This GAN is a core contribution and research output. For data, they used an existing large-scale dataset from the UK Biobank population study (85,709 adults' OCT images), which was not generated by the research team but is an existing resource used to train and validate their model (D2).

These simulated narratives constitute newly generated data (FTD-like text corpora) that are central to the research goals and are shared via an accompanying Python tutorial. Thus software is 'used' (S2) while data is 'generated' (D1).

The researchers will use an existing commercial platform (Qualtrics XM) to design and disseminate the survey - this is existing software used but not developed by the research team (S2). The study will generate new primary survey data from international participants on SSI prevention practices, which is new data collected specifically for this research (D1), even though at the protocol stage no data has yet been collected/shared.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis that synthesizes existing published studies and national survey data on adolescent nutrition in Ethiopia. The researchers used existing data (from 76 articles and 2 national surveys) to calculate pooled prevalence estimates, but did not generate new primary data themselves - they aggregated and analyzed pre-existing published data. No software tool was developed or is central to the paper; standard statistical meta-analysis methods were used but not described as newly developed software. Thus, this falls under Software Used/No Software (routine statistical analysis, not a substantial software contribution) and Data Used (existing published data compiled and analyzed).

The study generated new experimental data (HD-sEMG recordings and decomposed motor unit firing data) from 18 children performing handgrip contractions, which is new data collected specifically for this research and thus classified as D1. For software, the study used existing signal decomposition algorithms and analysis tools (e.g., EMG decomposition software) to process the surface EMG signals into motor unit action potential trains, but there is no indication that new software was developed or substantially extended as part of this research - they used established decomposition/analysis methods, placing it in S2 (Software Used).
